title: Quantifier elimination: equality patterns and dense orders

based_on.title: Model Theory Lecture Notes
based_on.pages: Corollary5.8, pp51–52, and Proposition6.16, p69 (updated2018-12-14); the compactness argument is expanded without type-space topology

summary: Characterize quantifier elimination by agreement of tuples, then eliminate equality and dense-order quantifiers and describe definable sets.
abstract: In the rational order, asking whether there is a point strictly between two given points is the same as asking whether the first is smaller than the second. Quantifier elimination extends this simplification to every formula of a theory. It holds precisely when tuples agreeing on every quantifier-free formula also agree on every formula; two uses of compactness turn that semantic test into a finite formula. For infinite sets with equality alone, formulas reduce to equality comparisons; for nonempty dense linear orders without endpoints, they reduce to comparisons of order and equality. This determines which subsets formulas can describe: finite or cofinite sets in the first case, and finite unions of intervals and points in the second, with parameters allowed. It also shows that all models of each example agree on sentences, and inclusions between its models preserve every formula with parameters.
